questions.question_en: This pavement marking indicates that vehicles may not pass through the area of the marking.
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. The depicted yellow-bordered road marking is a no-entry area (立入り禁止部分); vehicles must not enter the marked part.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Traffic signs and road markings communicate mandatory directions, prohibitions, warnings, and designated road areas. The exact shape, colour, line pattern, arrow, and supplementary plate matter.

PRACTICAL MEANING: While driving, use **Signs and road markings** to make sure the instruction is interpreted consistently before acting. Apply the rule before the manoeuvre begins; if the situation is uncertain, create extra time or space instead of assuming an exception.

EXAM TRAP: This is image-dependent. Identify the exact sign, marking, signal, line pattern, vehicle position, or road layout first; a similar-looking image can test a completely different rule.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

questions.question_en: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, drivers may keep your speed without slowing down if it is clear that there is no pedestrian that is crossing.
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. At a pedestrian crossing, you must slow enough to stop unless it is clearly evident that no pedestrian or bicycle is crossing or about to cross. If it is clearly empty, that slowdown duty does not apply.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Drivers must give special protection to pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, particularly at crossings, near children, and where visibility is restricted.

PRACTICAL MEANING: While driving, use **Protection of pedestrians** to protect pedestrians and cyclists before their path conflicts with the vehicle. Apply the rule before the manoeuvre begins; if the situation is uncertain, create extra time or space instead of assuming an exception.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute or permission wording “may”. A statement becomes false when it turns a limited rule into a blanket permission, exemption, or prohibition.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

questions.question_en: When stopping a vehicle, it is alright to brake strongly only once because hitting the brakes several times will disorient the vehicles behind.
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. The NPA guide recommends braking progressively and, where appropriate, using the brake several times; flashing brake lamps can warn following traffic. Sudden hard braking is only for unavoidable danger.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Choose a speed that is both legal and safe for visibility, grip, traffic, and stopping distance. Greater speed reduces time to react and increases stopping distance and impact severity.

PRACTICAL MEANING: While driving, use **Speed, stopping and control** to preserve enough time and distance to stop without abrupt control inputs. Apply the rule before the manoeuvre begins; if the situation is uncertain, create extra time or space instead of assuming an exception.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute or permission wording “only”. A statement becomes false when it turns a limited rule into a blanket permission, exemption, or prohibition.

questions.question_en: When proceeding to a road, make sure that other vehicles or pedestrians can safely proceed by following rules and keeping in mind the road and traffic rules.
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. Drivers must follow traffic rules and pay attention to surrounding road users so that everyone can travel safely.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Road rules are common safety rules intended to make every road user’s actions predictable. Personal confidence or light traffic does not create an exception.

PRACTICAL MEANING: While driving, use **General safe-driving rule** to make the vehicle’s movement predictable and preserve a usable safety margin. Apply the rule before the manoeuvre begins; if the situation is uncertain, create extra time or space instead of assuming an exception.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute or permission wording “can”. A statement becomes false when it turns a limited rule into a blanket permission, exemption, or prohibition.

questions.question_en: In general rules, vehicles should proceed through the left side of the center line if a center line is present.
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. Vehicles generally must travel on the left side of the road center, or left of the center line when one is present, subject to listed exceptions.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Keep the proper side/lane, obey lane-use markings, and change course only after checking that the move will not interfere with others.

PRACTICAL MEANING: While driving, use **Road position and lane use** to avoid entering another road user’s path unexpectedly. Apply the rule before the manoeuvre begins; if the situation is uncertain, create extra time or space instead of assuming an exception.

EXAM TRAP: Name the rule first: **Road position and lane use**. The distractor often sounds generally safe but changes one legal condition, exception, or required action.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

questions.rule_summary: Apply the traffic rule exactly as written and do not invent exceptions.

questions.explanation_detailed:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. These preparations help reduce harm and allow an appropriate response if an accident or emergency occurs.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Apply the traffic rule exactly as written and do not invent exceptions.

PRACTICAL MEANING: While driving, use **Core traffic rule** to prevent a secondary collision and reduce the severity of injury. Apply the rule before the manoeuvre begins; if the situation is uncertain, create extra time or space instead of assuming an exception.

EXAM TRAP: Name the rule first: **Core traffic rule**. The distractor often sounds generally safe but changes one legal condition, exception, or required action.

questions.question_en_exam: When driving, you should routinely prepare for emergencies by obtaining automobile insurance, learning first-aid procedures, and keeping emergency supplies in the vehicle.

questions.question_en: When crossing a railway crossing, you must stop immediately before it, or before the stop line if there is one, and check safety to both sides with your own eyes and ears, for example by opening a window or lowering the car-stereo volume.
questions.question_ja: 踏切を通過するときは、踏切の直前（停止線があるときは、その直前）で一時停止をし、車の窓を開けたり、カーステレオのボリュームを下げるなどして、自分の目と耳で左右の安全を確かめなければならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. The basic rule is to stop before the crossing and directly confirm that it is safe before entering.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend.

PRACTICAL MEANING: One train passing does not guarantee the crossing is clear; another train may approach from the opposite direction.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute or permission wording “must”. A statement becomes false when it turns a limited rule into a blanket permission, exemption, or prohibition.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

questions.question_en: Areas near road bends, near the crest of an uphill slope, and on steep downhill slopes are places where vehicles must proceed slowly.

ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. These are designated locations where a vehicle must slow down because visibility or vehicle control may be limited.

RULE TO REMEMBER: 徐行 means travelling at a speed at which the vehicle can stop immediately; it is not defined by a single universal kilometre-per-hour figure or by one-half of the posted speed limit.

PRACTICAL MEANING: If the statement invents a fixed numeric definition for 徐行, it is usually the trap.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute or permission wording “must”. A statement becomes false when it turns a limited rule into a blanket permission, exemption, or prohibition.

questions.question_en: If you hold an ordinary driver’s license, you may drive a cargo vehicle with a maximum load of 3,000 kilograms and a passenger vehicle with seating for 11 people.
questions.question_ja: 普通免許を受けていれば、最大積載量が3,000キログラムの貨物自動車、乗車定員11人の乗用自動車を運転することができる。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. An ordinary license does not cover a vehicle with an 11-person capacity, and its vehicle/load limits are lower than the figures stated.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Whether a goods vehicle can be driven on an ordinary licence depends on the current statutory vehicle-weight and payload thresholds and the date/type of licence held. Compare the stated gross weight and maximum payload with the applicable licence class limits.

PRACTICAL MEANING: These are precise numeric questions; one threshold being within range does not help if another threshold exceeds the licence limit.

EXAM TRAP: Check the exact number/threshold in the statement: 000キログラム.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

questions.question_en: When turning right at an intersection, except a roundabout, a motorcycle may travel straight from behind an oncoming vehicle and be hidden from view, so you must proceed with sufficient care.
questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）で右折しようとするときは、対向車のかげから二輪車が直進してくる場合があり、危険であるから十分に注意して通行しなければならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. An oncoming vehicle can conceal a motorcycle or other road user, so a right-turning driver must check carefully before crossing the oncoming path.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When entering a roundabout, slow down and do not obstruct vehicles already circulating. Travel along the edge of the roundabout and use signals according to the prescribed exit/turning method.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Do not apply ordinary intersection right-of-way rules mechanically to a roundabout.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute or permission wording “may”. A statement becomes false when it turns a limited rule into a blanket permission, exemption, or prohibition.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. A driver must concentrate on safe vehicle control and may not engage in distracting activity that interferes with driving.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, it is best to close the following distance to the vehicle ahead as much as possible, then accelerate hard and change course from immediately behind it.
questions.question_ja: 追越しをする場合は、前の車との車間距離をできるだけ詰めておいて、その直近から一気に加速して進路変更するのがよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. You should keep a safe following distance, check ahead and behind, and make a smooth, safe overtaking manoeuvre rather than closing dangerously on the vehicle ahead.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Keep enough distance to stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows suddenly. Increase the gap when speed is higher or when rain, snow, ice, poor visibility, or heavy vehicles increase risk.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A fixed following distance is not safe under every condition.

EXAM TRAP: Timing and sequence matter. Separate “in advance,” “about 3 seconds before,” “30 m before,” “immediately before,” and “after the manoeuvre”; the exam often swaps these.

SOURCE BASIS: This Karimen item retains its verified answer/explanation source and is also anchored to the official Japanese traffic-rule framework recorded in the question sources.

EXAM TRAP: Timing and sequence matter. Separate “in advance,” “about 3 seconds before,” “30 m before,” “immediately before,” and “after the manoeuvre”; the exam often swaps these.

questions.question_en: When passing near an intersection or pedestrian crossing, pedestrians may cross at any time, so you must always sound the horn.
questions.question_ja: 交差点付近や横断歩道を通る場合は、いつ歩行者が横断するかわからないので、必ず警音器を鳴らす必要がある。

ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. The horn may be used only when required by a horn sign or when necessary to avoid danger, not routinely at every intersection or crossing.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When a pedestrian or cyclist is crossing or is about to cross at a protected crossing, the driver must stop as necessary and must not obstruct the crossing. Unless it is clearly apparent that nobody is crossing or about to cross, approach at a speed that allows stopping before the crossing.

PRACTICAL MEANING: “No interference” does not mean you may simply creep through in front of someone who has crossing priority.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “必ず”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_ja: 交差点（環状交差点を除く）を左折するときは、左側に寄って通行する二輪車に十分注意し、あらかじめ道路の左端に寄り、徐行しながら巻き込み事故を起こさないよう運転する。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. Moving left in advance and checking the left side reduces the risk of trapping a bicycle or motorcycle between the vehicle and the curb during the turn.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Do not apply ordinary intersection right-of-way rules mechanically to a roundabout.

EXAM TRAP: Timing and sequence matter. Separate “in advance,” “about 3 seconds before,” “30 m before,” “immediately before,” and “after the manoeuvre”; the exam often swaps these.

ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

questions.question_en: At an unsignalized intersection, I saw a pedestrian begin crossing at a pedestrian crossing. The pedestrian stopped after seeing my car, so I slowed down and passed without stopping.
questions.question_ja: 信号のない交差点を直進しようとしたところ横断歩道を渡り始めた歩行者を認めたが、自分の運転する車を見て立ち止まったので、一時停止せずに徐行して通過した。
questions.explanation:

RULE TO REMEMBER: When a pedestrian or cyclist is crossing or is about to cross at a protected crossing, the driver must stop as necessary and must not obstruct the crossing. PRACTICAL MEANING: “No interference” does not mean you may simply creep through in front of someone who has crossing priority.

EXAM TRAP: Timing and sequence matter. Separate “in advance,” “about 3 seconds before,” “30 m before,” “immediately before,” and “after the manoeuvre”; the exam often swaps these.

ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Hazards at an accident scene**, especially the traffic-accident duty. The governing rule is: At an accident scene, fuel leakage, fire, unstable cargo, and hazardous materials can create a second emergency. Approach carefully, keep ignition sources away, warn traffic, and call emergency services when necessary. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At an accident scene, fuel leakage, fire, unstable cargo, and hazardous materials can create a second emergency. Approach carefully, keep ignition sources away, warn traffic, and call emergency services when necessary.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A crash scene may be dangerous even after the vehicles have stopped.

questions.question_en: Although the condition section of the driver's license stated "Ordinary vehicles: AT vehicles only," I drove a manual-transmission vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 免許証の条件欄に「普通車はAT車に限る」と記載されていたが、マニュアル車を運転した。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **AT-only licence condition**, especially the precise condition and wording used in the statement. The governing rule is: A licence condition such as “ordinary vehicles limited to AT” must be obeyed. Driving a manual vehicle outside that condition is not permitted. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A licence condition such as “ordinary vehicles limited to AT” must be obeyed. Driving a manual vehicle outside that condition is not permitted.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A licence condition is a legal restriction, not a recommendation.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **AT-only licence condition** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: Because the maximum speed was not restricted by signs or other means on a national expressway, I drove a large motorcycle at 120 km/h.
questions.question_ja: 高速自動車国道で標識などにより最高速度が制限されていなかったので、大型自動二輪車で時速120キロメートルで走行した。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Maximum-speed sign**, especially the applicable maximum-speed rule, the national expressway rule, the exact traffic sign and the motorcycle-specific rule. The governing rule is: A maximum-speed sign states the legal upper limit for vehicles to which it applies. The driver must still choose a lower speed when weather, visibility, traffic, or road conditions make the posted maximum unsafe. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A maximum-speed sign states the legal upper limit for vehicles to which it applies. The driver must still choose a lower speed when weather, visibility, traffic, or road conditions make the posted maximum unsafe.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A posted maximum is not a target speed and is different from a minimum-speed sign.

EXAM TRAP: Check the exact number/threshold in the statement: 120キロメートル.

questions.question_en: When riding a motorcycle around a corner or curve, it is good to adjust your speed while applying the brakes as you turn.
questions.question_ja: 二輪車で曲がり角やカーブを走行するときは、ブレーキをかけながら速度を調節して曲がるとよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Motorcycle cornering**, especially the motorcycle-specific rule, the braking rule and the curve/cornering rule. The governing rule is: For a motorcycle, reduce speed before the curve, look through the turn, keep a stable posture, and use smooth throttle/brake/steering inputs. Abrupt braking in the curve can destabilize the motorcycle. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: For a motorcycle, reduce speed before the curve, look through the turn, keep a stable posture, and use smooth throttle/brake/steering inputs. Abrupt braking in the curve can destabilize the motorcycle.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The exam often tests when to slow: before entering the curve, not after discovering you are too fast mid-corner.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Motorcycle cornering** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: On an expressway, the following distance may be the same on a dry road surface and on a road surface wet from rain or other causes.
questions.question_ja: 高速道路での車間距離は、乾いた路面のときと雨などでぬれているときは同じでよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Following distance**, especially the expressway rule, the following-distance requirement and the wet-weather rule. The governing rule is: Keep enough distance to stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows suddenly. Increase the gap when speed is higher or when rain, snow, ice, poor visibility, or heavy vehicles increase risk. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Keep enough distance to stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows suddenly. Increase the gap when speed is higher or when rain, snow, ice, poor visibility, or heavy vehicles increase risk.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A fixed following distance is not safe under every condition.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “同じでよい”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_en: Because using a mobile phone while driving is dangerous, it is good to switch it off or set it to driving mode before driving so that the call alert does not sound.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転中の携帯電話の使用は危険であるから、運転する前に電源を切ったり、ドライブモードにするなどして呼出音が鳴らないようにしておくのがよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Mobile phone distraction**, especially the mobile-phone restriction. The governing rule is: Using or handling a mobile phone while driving can take the driver’s eyes, hands, and attention away from traffic. Arrange calls/navigation before moving and stop in a safe place when operation is necessary. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Using or handling a mobile phone while driving can take the driver’s eyes, hands, and attention away from traffic. Arrange calls/navigation before moving and stop in a safe place when operation is necessary.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The question is about attention and control, not merely whether the vehicle is moving fast.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Mobile phone distraction** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: If a vehicle trying to overtake from behind has a lower maximum legal speed than your vehicle, you do not have to give way.
questions.question_ja: 後方から追越そうとしている車が自分の車より最高速度（法定速度）の低い車であれば、進路をゆずらなくてもよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Do not obstruct a vehicle overtaking you**, especially the applicable maximum-speed rule, the statutory-speed rule and the overtaking rule. The governing rule is: When another vehicle is lawfully overtaking, do not increase speed or otherwise obstruct the pass; facilitate a safe return where the road situation requires it. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When another vehicle is lawfully overtaking, do not increase speed or otherwise obstruct the pass; facilitate a safe return where the road situation requires it.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The overtaking vehicle having a lower statutory maximum speed does not give you permission to block an otherwise lawful pass.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Do not obstruct a vehicle overtaking you** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

Merely remaining in the driver’s seat does not prevent a continuous stop from being “parking.” Short passenger pickup/drop-off and loading/unloading within the legal definition may be “stopping” instead. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Parking includes continuous stopping and also stopping when the driver leaves the vehicle and cannot immediately drive it. Merely remaining in the driver’s seat does not prevent a continuous stop from being “parking.” Short passenger pickup/drop-off and loading/unloading within the legal definition may be “stopping” instead.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The key is the nature/duration/purpose of the stop, not simply whether the driver is sitting inside.

questions.question_en: When it is unavoidable to brake on an expressway, it is good to use engine braking and press the brake pedal several times in separate applications.

The governing rule is: Brake early and smoothly in normal driving. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Brake early and smoothly in normal driving. Where strong braking is necessary, keep the vehicle stable and use the braking method appropriate to the vehicle and road surface; repeated pedal application can also alert following traffic on vehicles without a dedicated emergency-stop signal.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Do not turn a recommended technique into a universal rule for every modern braking system or every emergency.

questions.question_en: When traveling on a road with this road marking, it indicates that the intersecting road ahead is a priority road.
questions.question_ja: この標示がある道路を進行しているときは、この先の交差する道路が優先道路になっていることを示している。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Priority-road-ahead road marking**, especially the exact road marking. The governing rule is: The triangular road markings shown warn that the road ahead at the intersection is the priority road, so the driver on the present approach must prepare to yield/slow as required. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: The triangular road markings shown warn that the road ahead at the intersection is the priority road, so the driver on the present approach must prepare to yield/slow as required.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The marking is an advance warning about priority at the upcoming intersection, not a declaration that your present road has priority.

EXAM TRAP: This is an image-dependent item: identify the exact sign/marking/signal shown before applying the rule; similar-looking symbols can have different meanings.

questions.question_en: At night on an expressway, the tail lamps of ordinary and large vehicles are easy to notice, but motorcycle tail lamps are small and difficult to see, so there is a danger of misjudging the distance and care is necessary.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Lights at night**, especially the expressway rule, the motorcycle-specific rule and the night-driving rule. The governing rule is: Use the required lights at night and when visibility is poor. When stopped on an expressway because of breakdown or emergency, make the vehicle conspicuous and use the required warning equipment as well. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Use the required lights at night and when visibility is poor. When stopped on an expressway because of breakdown or emergency, make the vehicle conspicuous and use the required warning equipment as well.

PRACTICAL MEANING: One warning device does not necessarily replace the other required lights or warning triangle/device.

questions.question_en: Radiator water is used to cool the engine, so during the low-temperature winter season it is not necessary to inspect it or replenish the water.
questions.question_ja: ラジエータの水はエンジンを冷やすためのものであるから、温度の低い冬期は、点検をしたり、水を補給する必要はない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Cooling system / overheating**, especially the absolute phrase “no need”. The governing rule is: Check coolant as part of vehicle maintenance in all seasons. If overheating occurs, stop safely and follow the vehicle’s procedure; do not open a pressurized cooling system or pour water onto a hot engine carelessly. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Check coolant as part of vehicle maintenance in all seasons. If overheating occurs, stop safely and follow the vehicle’s procedure; do not open a pressurized cooling system or pour water onto a hot engine carelessly.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Cold weather does not eliminate the need for coolant, and a hot cooling system can cause severe burns.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “必要はない”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_en: This sign indicates a place where there is a center line, but the center line is not necessarily located at the physical center of the road.
questions.question_ja: この標識は、道路の中央線のあるところを示しているが、中央線は必ずしも道路の中央にあるとは限らない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Center line and yellow line**, especially the exact traffic sign, the centre-line restriction and the absolute word “must/always”. The governing rule is: A center line separates opposing directions. When the applicable center line is a solid yellow line restricting right-side entry for overtaking, a driver must not cross it merely to overtake. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A center line separates opposing directions. When the applicable center line is a solid yellow line restricting right-side entry for overtaking, a driver must not cross it merely to overtake.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The center line is not always geometrically in the exact center of the pavement.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “必ず”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule. This is an image-dependent item: identify the exact sign/marking/signal shown before applying the rule; similar-looking symbols can have different meanings.

questions.question_en: When a vehicle turns on a curve, centrifugal force acts on it and the vehicle tends to move toward the outside of the curve.
questions.question_ja: カーブを曲がるときは、遠心力が働き、自動車はカーブの外側に飛び出そうとする。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Centrifugal effect in curves**, especially the curve/cornering rule. The governing rule is: In a curve, the vehicle tends to move toward the outside. The effect becomes stronger as speed increases and as the curve becomes tighter, so enter at an appropriate speed and steer smoothly. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: In a curve, the vehicle tends to move toward the outside. The effect becomes stronger as speed increases and as the curve becomes tighter, so enter at an appropriate speed and steer smoothly.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Speed has a strong effect; a small increase can markedly reduce the safety margin.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Centrifugal effect in curves** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Pedestrians at crossings**, especially the pedestrian-crossing rule and the claimed permission/possibility. The governing rule is: When a pedestrian or cyclist is crossing or is about to cross at a protected crossing, the driver must stop as necessary and must not obstruct the crossing. Unless it is clearly apparent that nobody is crossing or about to cross, approach at a speed that allows stopping before the crossing. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When a pedestrian or cyclist is crossing or is about to cross at a protected crossing, the driver must stop as necessary and must not obstruct the crossing. Unless it is clearly apparent that nobody is crossing or about to cross, approach at a speed that allows stopping before the crossing.

PRACTICAL MEANING: “No interference” does not mean you may simply creep through in front of someone who has crossing priority.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the claimed permission/possibility. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

questions.question_en: If you cause a traffic accident, in addition to liability for damages to the victim, you may bear criminal and administrative responsibility.
questions.question_ja: 交通事故を起こした場合、被害者に対する損害賠償のほかに、刑事上、行政上の責任を負うことになる。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Responsibilities after a traffic crash**, especially the traffic-accident duty. The governing rule is: A traffic crash can create separate civil, criminal, and administrative consequences depending on the facts. Insurance may pay covered losses, but it does not automatically assume every civil responsibility or erase the driver’s other legal responsibilities. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A traffic crash can create separate civil, criminal, and administrative consequences depending on the facts. Insurance may pay covered losses, but it does not automatically assume every civil responsibility or erase the driver’s other legal responsibilities.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Do not collapse civil compensation, criminal liability, administrative licence action, and insurance into one concept.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Responsibilities after a traffic crash** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A vehicle owner or person providing a vehicle can bear responsibility when careless management or knowingly lending the vehicle enables unsafe or unlawful driving. Secure keys and do not provide a vehicle to an unfit or unlicensed driver.

questions.question_en: Because serious accidents can easily occur at railroad crossings, you must stop immediately before the crossing (or immediately before the stop line when there is one) to confirm safety.
questions.question_ja: 踏切では大きな事故が起こりやすいので、安全確認のため、踏切の直前（停止線があるときは、停止線の直前）で一時停止しなければならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Railroad crossing**, especially whether a complete stop is required, the railroad-crossing rule and the timing word “immediately before”. The governing rule is: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend.

PRACTICAL MEANING: One train passing does not guarantee the crossing is clear; another train may approach from the opposite direction.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the timing word “immediately before”. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

questions.question_en: On a snowy or frozen road, if snow tires such as studless tires or tire chains are fitted, you may drive in the same way as on a road in summer conditions.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Snow and ice**, especially the snow/ice rule. The governing rule is: On snow or ice, traction is greatly reduced. Fit appropriate winter equipment where required, reduce speed, increase following distance, and make steering, acceleration, and braking smooth. Tracks left by other vehicles may sometimes offer a more stable path, but can also be polished/icy, so judge the actual surface. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: On snow or ice, traction is greatly reduced. Fit appropriate winter equipment where required, reduce speed, increase following distance, and make steering, acceleration, and braking smooth. Tracks left by other vehicles may sometimes offer a more stable path, but can also be polished/icy, so judge the actual surface.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Winter tyres/chains reduce risk; they do not make winter roads behave like dry summer pavement.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “同じでよい”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Close a vehicle door in a controlled way: bring it close to the latch first, then close it firmly enough to engage. Confirm it is fully latched before moving.

questions.question_en: When driving, it is important not to think only of yourself but to respect the position of pedestrians and other drivers and to have a spirit of giving way and consideration.
questions.question_ja: 自動車を運転するときは、自分本位でなく歩行者やほかの運転者の立場も尊重し、ゆずり合いと思いやりの気持ちを持つことが大切である。

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Courtesy and cooperative driving**, especially the precise condition and wording used in the statement. The governing rule is: Safe traffic depends on predictable rule-following plus consideration for other road users. Yield and cooperate where required, avoid forcing your way through, and anticipate that another road user may make a mistake. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Safe traffic depends on predictable rule-following plus consideration for other road users. Yield and cooperate where required, avoid forcing your way through, and anticipate that another road user may make a mistake.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Courtesy does not mean surrendering legal priority blindly, but “self-centred driving is safer” is never the rule.

questions.explanation:

The governing rule is: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend.

PRACTICAL MEANING: One train passing does not guarantee the crossing is clear; another train may approach from the opposite direction.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the timing word “immediately before”. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A vehicle owner or person providing a vehicle can bear responsibility when careless management or knowingly lending the vehicle enables unsafe or unlawful driving. Secure keys and do not provide a vehicle to an unfit or unlicensed driver.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Responsibility is not always limited to the person holding the steering wheel.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “全く”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_en: When a vehicle ahead is stopped or proceeding slowly at an intersection, railroad crossing, or similar place, you must not cut in or cross in front of that vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 前方の車が交差点や踏切などで停止や徐行しているときは、その前に割り込んだり、横切ったりしてはならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Railroad crossing**, especially whether slow-speed/ready-to-stop driving is required and the railroad-crossing rule. The governing rule is: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At a railroad crossing, stop immediately before the crossing or stop line and confirm safety with your own eyes and ears. If a traffic signal controls the crossing, you may pass according to that signal. Never enter when the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to descend.

PRACTICAL MEANING: One train passing does not guarantee the crossing is clear; another train may approach from the opposite direction.

EXAM TRAP: The exam is testing whether **Railroad crossing** creates a prohibition, permission, or exception. Do not infer permission merely because the manoeuvre seems convenient or harmless.

questions.question_en: You must not park or stop alongside a vehicle that is already parked or stopped parallel to the road (double parking/stopping).

questions.question_en: On an expressway it is dangerous to stop on the main roadway or suddenly change course because you are unsure of your destination, so it is important to plan your route in advance.
questions.question_ja: 高速道路で走行中、行き先に迷って本線車道で停止したり、突然進路を変えたりすると危険なので、あらかじめ計画を立てることが大切である。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Plan an expressway route in advance**, especially the expressway rule. The governing rule is: Confirm the route and exits before entering an expressway. If uncertain while driving, continue safely and use a service area, parking area, or next exit rather than stopping suddenly or making an abrupt lane change. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Confirm the route and exits before entering an expressway. If uncertain while driving, continue safely and use a service area, parking area, or next exit rather than stopping suddenly or making an abrupt lane change.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Missing an exit is safer than making a sudden correction at highway speed.

EXAM TRAP: Timing is the trap. Distinguish “in advance,” “about 3 seconds before,” “30 m before,” “immediately before,” and “after the manoeuvre”; they are not interchangeable.

questions.question_ja: 二輪車でぬかるみや砂利道を走行するときは、ブレーキをかけたり大きなハンドル操作はせずに、スロットルで速度を変化させながら走行するとよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Motorcycle on loose/poor surfaces**, especially the motorcycle-specific rule and the braking rule. The governing rule is: On mud, gravel, or other low-grip surfaces, reduce speed beforehand, keep the motorcycle stable, avoid abrupt braking/steering/throttle changes, and choose a smooth path. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: On mud, gravel, or other low-grip surfaces, reduce speed beforehand, keep the motorcycle stable, avoid abrupt braking/steering/throttle changes, and choose a smooth path.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Do not try to “power through” with abrupt throttle changes or large steering inputs.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Motorcycle on loose/poor surfaces** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Starting an automatic car**, especially the reversing rule, the automatic-vehicle operating rule and the braking rule. The governing rule is: Before moving an automatic car, hold the brake firmly, confirm the selector position visually, select the intended range, check surroundings, release the parking brake as appropriate, and move off smoothly. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Before moving an automatic car, hold the brake firmly, confirm the selector position visually, select the intended range, check surroundings, release the parking brake as appropriate, and move off smoothly.

PRACTICAL MEANING: AT convenience does not remove the risk of selecting the wrong range or unintended creep.

questions.question_en: At night, it is good to direct your eyes farther ahead so that you can discover and avoid obstacles early.
questions.question_ja: 夜間は、先の方に視線を向け、前方の障害を早く発見して避けるようにするとよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Night-time visual search**, especially the night-driving rule. The governing rule is: At night, visible range and contrast are reduced. Look well ahead within the illuminated area, scan for pedestrians and unlit hazards, control speed so you can stop within what you can see, and avoid staring only at the road immediately in front. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At night, visible range and contrast are reduced. Look well ahead within the illuminated area, scan for pedestrians and unlit hazards, control speed so you can stop within what you can see, and avoid staring only at the road immediately in front.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Light traffic does not compensate for the shorter seeing distance at night.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Night-time visual search** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: When turning right or left at an intersection with little traffic (except a roundabout), it is acceptable to give the signal only immediately before the turn.
questions.question_ja: 交通量の少ない交差点（環状交差点を除く）を右左折するときの合図の時期は、その直前でもよい。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Turn signal timing**, especially the left-turn rule and the timing word “immediately before”. The governing rule is: Signal early enough for other road users to understand your intention: normally from about 30 metres before the turning point, and cancel the signal promptly after completing the manoeuvre. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Signal early enough for other road users to understand your intention: normally from about 30 metres before the turning point, and cancel the signal promptly after completing the manoeuvre.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Signalling only as the steering wheel begins to turn is too late.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the timing word “immediately before”. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

questions.question_en: When driving, obeying traffic rules is the basic requirement for safe road use, but if you are confident that you will not cause an accident, it is not always necessary to obey them.
questions.question_ja: 車を運転する場合、交通規則を守ることは道路を安全に通行するための基本であるが、事故を起こさない自信があれば必ずしも守る必要はない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Rules, courtesy and defensive driving**, especially the absolute phrase “no need” and the absolute word “must/always”. The governing rule is: Obeying traffic rules is the minimum framework for safe road use. Good driving also requires consideration for others and anticipating mistakes; confidence does not justify ignoring rules or courtesy. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Obeying traffic rules is the minimum framework for safe road use. Good driving also requires consideration for others and anticipating mistakes; confidence does not justify ignoring rules or courtesy.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Statements that replace common rules with personal confidence are false.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “必ず”, “必要はない”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_en: If you collide with a concrete wall at 60 km/h, the impact is approximately equivalent to falling from a height of about 14 meters (roughly the fifth floor of a building).
questions.question_ja: 時速60キロメートルでコンクリートの壁に激突した場合は、約14メートルの高さ（ビルの5階程度）から落ちた場合と同じ程度の衝撃力を受ける。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Collision energy**, especially the stated 60 km value and the stated 14 m value. The governing rule is: Impact severity rises rapidly with speed. Doubling speed greatly increases kinetic energy, so even a moderate increase in speed can make a crash far more severe. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Impact severity rises rapidly with speed. Doubling speed greatly increases kinetic energy, so even a moderate increase in speed can make a crash far more severe.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The exact analogy in a question is secondary to the core point: speed has a disproportionate effect on crash energy.

EXAM TRAP: Check the exact number/threshold in the statement: 60キロメートル, 14メートル.

ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Driving in multiple lanes**, especially the lane-use rule. The governing rule is: On a road with multiple lanes in the same direction, use the lanes according to the keep-left/lane-use rules and any signs or markings. The rightmost lane is not simply a free-choice cruising lane. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: On a road with multiple lanes in the same direction, use the lanes according to the keep-left/lane-use rules and any signs or markings. The rightmost lane is not simply a free-choice cruising lane.

questions.question_en: When passing through an intersection with poor visibility, there is danger of overlooking another vehicle or of a pedestrian suddenly entering the road, so it is necessary to proceed slowly and carefully.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Passing pedestrians**, especially whether slow-speed/ready-to-stop driving is required. The governing rule is: When passing close to a pedestrian, leave a safe lateral interval or slow down sufficiently. This protection also matters on roads without a sidewalk and beside roadside strips. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When passing close to a pedestrian, leave a safe lateral interval or slow down sufficiently. This protection also matters on roads without a sidewalk and beside roadside strips.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A roadside strip does not make close passing automatically safe.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Passing pedestrians** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: When a traffic accident occurs, the driver must report to a police officer the place of the accident, the number and condition of injured persons, the extent of property damage, cargo carried by the accident vehicle, and other required matters, and receive instructions.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Accident reporting duty**, especially the police-officer signal/instruction, the loading/cargo restriction, the traffic-accident duty and the injured-person/first-aid rule. The governing rule is: When a traffic accident occurs, the driver must stop, take measures to prevent further danger, help injured persons as necessary, and report the required facts to the police. This duty does not disappear merely because the other party caused the accident. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When a traffic accident occurs, the driver must stop, take measures to prevent further danger, help injured persons as necessary, and report the required facts to the police. This duty does not disappear merely because the other party caused the accident.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Fault is decided separately from the immediate post-accident duties. Do not confuse “who caused it” with “whether you must stop, help, and report.”

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Accident reporting duty** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Absolute safety rules are frequently tested using excuses such as “only a little,” “I am confident,” or “it was last night.”

questions.question_en: Vision decreases when you suddenly move from a bright place into a dark place, but it does not change when moving from a dark place into a bright place.

ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Dark/light adaptation**, especially the precise condition and wording used in the statement. RULE TO REMEMBER: Vision temporarily deteriorates when the eyes must adapt to a large change in brightness—both when entering darkness and after leaving a very bright area. Reduce speed and allow time for adaptation.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The trap is claiming that adaptation occurs in only one direction.

questions.question_en: Whenever a vehicle remains stopped continuously for loading or unloading cargo, the stop is always regarded as parking.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Good observation means looking well ahead while repeatedly scanning near, far, left, right, mirrors, and potential conflict areas. Do not fix the eyes on a single point, but also do not look so vaguely that specific hazards are missed.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The safe answer is active scanning—not tunnel vision and not unfocused “looking at everything.”

ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Snow and ice**, especially the braking rule and the snow/ice rule. The governing rule is: On snow or ice, traction is greatly reduced. Fit appropriate winter equipment where required, reduce speed, increase following distance, and make steering, acceleration, and braking smooth. Tracks left by other vehicles may sometimes offer a more stable path, but can also be polished/icy, so judge the actual surface. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: On snow or ice, traction is greatly reduced. Fit appropriate winter equipment where required, reduce speed, increase following distance, and make steering, acceleration, and braking smooth. Tracks left by other vehicles may sometimes offer a more stable path, but can also be polished/icy, so judge the actual surface.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Winter tyres/chains reduce risk; they do not make winter roads behave like dry summer pavement.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Snow and ice** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

The governing rule is: At night, visible range and contrast are reduced. Look well ahead within the illuminated area, scan for pedestrians and unlit hazards, control speed so you can stop within what you can see, and avoid staring only at the road immediately in front. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: At night, visible range and contrast are reduced. Look well ahead within the illuminated area, scan for pedestrians and unlit hazards, control speed so you can stop within what you can see, and avoid staring only at the road immediately in front.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Light traffic does not compensate for the shorter seeing distance at night.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the claimed permission/possibility. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

questions.explanation:

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Yielding to emergency vehicles**, especially the exact traffic sign, the exact road marking and the lane-use rule. The governing rule is: When an emergency vehicle approaches, avoid blocking an intersection. Near an intersection, clear it and stop at the left side as required; elsewhere, move to the left and give the emergency vehicle a clear path. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When an emergency vehicle approaches, avoid blocking an intersection. Near an intersection, clear it and stop at the left side as required; elsewhere, move to the left and give the emergency vehicle a clear path.

The governing rule is: Children, elderly persons, wheelchair users, and people using guide dogs or white/yellow canes may need extra space and time. PRACTICAL MEANING: The exam tests anticipation: do not wait for a person to step directly into the vehicle’s path before reacting.

questions.question_en: Not only sudden starts, sudden braking, and racing the engine, but also leaving the engine idling during a continuous stop, can cause unnecessary fuel consumption.

The governing rule is: Brake early and smoothly in normal driving. RULE TO REMEMBER: Brake early and smoothly in normal driving. Where strong braking is necessary, keep the vehicle stable and use the braking method appropriate to the vehicle and road surface; repeated pedal application can also alert following traffic on vehicles without a dedicated emergency-stop signal.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Do not turn a recommended technique into a universal rule for every modern braking system or every emergency.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “だけで”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

The governing rule is: If engine speed cannot be reduced because of a fault, disconnect drive by selecting neutral as appropriate, brake to a safe stop, then shut the engine down once the vehicle can be controlled safely. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: If engine speed cannot be reduced because of a fault, disconnect drive by selecting neutral as appropriate, brake to a safe stop, then shut the engine down once the vehicle can be controlled safely.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The priority is separating engine power from the wheels and stopping under control; do not continue driving against uncontrolled engine power.

questions.question_en: Even if a traffic accident occurs, when you are not at fault and the accident was caused by the other party's negligence, you have no duty to report it to the police.

ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

questions.question_en: Even when a vehicle remains stopped continuously at a place where parking is prohibited, it is not considered parking if the driver remains inside the vehicle.
questions.question_ja: 駐車禁止の場所に継続して停止するような場合でも、運転者が車の中にいれば駐車にはならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. The uploaded practice page's key was overridden because it conflicts with the official rule. Parking includes a continuous stop; remaining inside the vehicle does not automatically turn a continuing stop into mere stopping.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Whether a stop is legally “parking” depends on purpose, duration, and whether the vehicle is continuously stopped—not simply on whether the driver remains seated inside.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Sitting in the driver seat does not convert a continuing parking-type stop into lawful stopping.

EXAM TRAP: The exam is testing whether **Driver presence does not decide parking** creates a prohibition, permission, or exception. Do not infer permission merely because the manoeuvre seems convenient or harmless.

questions.question_en: When stopping a vehicle, you should always pay attention to following traffic and take measures to avoid being struck from behind, such as applying the brakes several times or extending an arm diagonally downward outside the vehicle to give a stopping signal.
questions.question_ja: 車を停止させるときは、追突されないようにブレーキを数回に分けて踏んだり、腕を車の外に出して、斜め下にのばして停止の合図を行うなど、常に後続車の動きに注意することが必要である。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The correct answer is **TRUE / 正解**. The uploaded practice page's key was overridden because it conflicts with the official rule. Using the brake in several applications can illuminate the brake lamps repeatedly and help warn following traffic when slowing/stopping; the driver must also monitor following vehicles.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When slowing/stopping, monitor following traffic and give a clear early indication. Brake-lamp activation and, where legally applicable, the prescribed hand signal can communicate deceleration/stopping.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The safety point is early, clear communication plus controlled braking—not merely pressing the pedal once at the last moment.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “常に”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_en: When overtaking, a sudden acceleration or sudden steering movement to change course can cause the steering to be pulled or the vehicle to skid sideways, so sufficient care is necessary.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Avoid abrupt inputs. When the rear begins to slide, steer smoothly in the direction needed to regain alignment while easing the cause of the skid; an abrupt opposite steering input can worsen loss of control.

questions.question_en: A pedestrian was in a safety zone, so I proceeded slowly while passing.
questions.question_ja: 安全地帯に歩行者がいたので、徐行して通行した。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Passing pedestrians**, especially whether slow-speed/ready-to-stop driving is required and the safety-zone rule. The governing rule is: When passing close to a pedestrian, leave a safe lateral interval or slow down sufficiently. This protection also matters on roads without a sidewalk and beside roadside strips. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: When passing close to a pedestrian, leave a safe lateral interval or slow down sufficiently. This protection also matters on roads without a sidewalk and beside roadside strips.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A roadside strip does not make close passing automatically safe.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Passing pedestrians** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: On a road with this sign, carrying a passenger on a large motorcycle or ordinary motorcycle is prohibited.
questions.question_ja: この標識のある道路では、大型自動二輪車、普通自動二輪車の二人乗り通行を禁止している。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Motorcycle carrying a passenger**, especially the exact traffic sign and the motorcycle-specific rule. The governing rule is: Passenger-carrying on a motorcycle is subject to licence-experience and road-specific restrictions. Expressway passenger carrying has stricter age/experience requirements than ordinary-road riding. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Passenger-carrying on a motorcycle is subject to licence-experience and road-specific restrictions. Expressway passenger carrying has stricter age/experience requirements than ordinary-road riding.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Check both the rider’s age/experience and whether the road itself permits two-person riding.

EXAM TRAP: This is an image-dependent item: identify the exact sign/marking/signal shown before applying the rule; similar-looking symbols can have different meanings.

questions.question_en: Because motorcycles are highly maneuverable and can turn in a small space, they may overtake the vehicle ahead even when that vehicle is changing course to the right for a right turn or other reason.
questions.question_ja: 二輪車は、機動性に富み小回りがきくので、前の車が右折などのため進路を変えようとしているときであっても、これを追越すことができる。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The correct answer is **FALSE / 不正解**. The uploaded practice page's key was overridden because it conflicts with the official rule. A motorcycle may not use its manoeuvrability to overtake a vehicle on the prohibited side while that vehicle is moving right for a right turn.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A motorcycle’s agility does not permit a pass that conflicts with a vehicle ahead moving right for a right turn/course change. Respect the turning vehicle’s path and avoid entering the conflict area.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Vehicle agility never creates an exception to an overtaking prohibition/right-turn conflict.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the claimed permission/possibility. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

questions.question_en: Near the top of an uphill slope, you must not overtake even when the vehicle ahead is traveling slowly.
questions.question_ja: 上り坂の頂上付近では、前の車が遅い速度で走っていても追越してはならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Places where overtaking is prohibited**, especially the overtaking rule and the hill/gradient rule. The governing rule is: Overtaking is prohibited at designated dangerous locations such as road corners and near the crest of a hill, and at other places specified by signs or law. A slow vehicle ahead does not cancel the prohibition. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Overtaking is prohibited at designated dangerous locations such as road corners and near the crest of a hill, and at other places specified by signs or law. A slow vehicle ahead does not cancel the prohibition.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The trap is an invented exception based on impatience, low speed, or light traffic.

EXAM TRAP: The exam is testing whether **Places where overtaking is prohibited** creates a prohibition, permission, or exception. Do not infer permission merely because the manoeuvre seems convenient or harmless.

questions.question_en: A person was crossing a pedestrian crossing, but when my vehicle approached the person stopped walking, so I continued driving without stopping.
questions.question_ja: 横断歩道を横断している人がいたが、車が近づいたら立ち止まったので、そのまま進行を続けた。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Pedestrian remains protected while crossing**, especially the pedestrian-crossing rule. The governing rule is: A pedestrian who is on a crosswalk retains protection even if the person hesitates or momentarily stops because a vehicle approaches. Stop and allow the person to cross without intimidation or obstruction. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A pedestrian who is on a crosswalk retains protection even if the person hesitates or momentarily stops because a vehicle approaches. Stop and allow the person to cross without intimidation or obstruction.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A pedestrian stopping in fear is not a signal that the vehicle may take priority.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Pedestrian remains protected while crossing** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Overtaking in tunnels**, especially the overtaking rule and the lane-use rule. The governing rule is: Overtaking is prohibited in a tunnel without vehicle lanes. In a tunnel with lanes, apply the ordinary overtaking rules and any signs/markings. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Overtaking is prohibited in a tunnel without vehicle lanes. In a tunnel with lanes, apply the ordinary overtaking rules and any signs/markings.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The presence or absence of marked vehicle lanes is the key distinction.

questions.question_en: A police officer directing traffic at an intersection gave a "Stop" hand signal, so I stopped immediately before the stop line.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Police officer signals**, especially the police-officer signal/instruction, the traffic-signal rule and the timing word “immediately before”. The governing rule is: Signals given by a police officer or traffic controller must be obeyed. Their meaning depends on the officer’s body/arm/light direction relative to the road user, and they take precedence when they conflict with ordinary traffic lights. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Signals given by a police officer or traffic controller must be obeyed. Their meaning depends on the officer’s body/arm/light direction relative to the road user, and they take precedence when they conflict with ordinary traffic lights.

PRACTICAL MEANING: For diagram questions, identify your direction relative to the officer before deciding whether the indication is equivalent to green, yellow, or red.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the timing word “immediately before”. Licence questions often turn a limited rule into an absolute permission, exemption, or prohibition; check whether the stated exception actually exists.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Meaning of parking**, especially the parking rule. The governing rule is: Parking includes continuous stopping and also stopping when the driver leaves the vehicle and cannot immediately drive it. Merely remaining in the driver’s seat does not prevent a continuous stop from being “parking.” Short passenger pickup/drop-off and loading/unloading within the legal definition may be “stopping” instead. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Parking includes continuous stopping and also stopping when the driver leaves the vehicle and cannot immediately drive it. Merely remaining in the driver’s seat does not prevent a continuous stop from being “parking.” Short passenger pickup/drop-off and loading/unloading within the legal definition may be “stopping” instead.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The key is the nature/duration/purpose of the stop, not simply whether the driver is sitting inside.

EXAM TRAP: Identify **Meaning of parking** before answering. The distractor usually borrows a rule that is valid in a similar situation but not under the exact condition described here.

questions.question_en: The creep phenomenon in an automatic-transmission vehicle means that if the brake pedal is not firmly depressed, the vehicle may begin moving slowly even without pressing the accelerator pedal.

ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Recovering from a skid**, especially the precise condition and wording used in the statement. The governing rule is: Avoid abrupt inputs. When the rear begins to slide, steer smoothly in the direction needed to regain alignment while easing the cause of the skid; an abrupt opposite steering input can worsen loss of control. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Avoid abrupt inputs. When the rear begins to slide, steer smoothly in the direction needed to regain alignment while easing the cause of the skid; an abrupt opposite steering input can worsen loss of control.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The exact recovery depends on vehicle behaviour, but “jerk the wheel the opposite way” is not a safe general rule.

questions.question_en: To turn a curve safely, it is better to reduce speed sufficiently on the straight section before the curve rather than slow down while already in the curve.

RULE TO REMEMBER: Reduce to a safe speed before entering a curve, then maintain stable control through it. Heavy braking or abrupt steering in the middle of a curve can upset vehicle balance and increase the risk of skidding.

PRACTICAL MEANING: The key timing is “before the curve,” not waiting until the vehicle is already committed to the turn.

The governing rule is: When a pedestrian or cyclist is crossing or is about to cross at a protected crossing, the driver must stop as necessary and must not obstruct the crossing. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

questions.question_en: The intersection signal changed to yellow. I could have stopped safely, but because a yellow signal does not mean "Stop," I proceeded through carefully.

The governing rule is: A steady yellow signal generally means stop at the stopping position if this can be done safely; a vehicle already so close that it cannot stop safely may continue through. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

questions.question_en: Even at a place where parking is prohibited, a stop for loading or unloading cargo is never considered parking regardless of how long it lasts.
questions.question_ja: 駐車禁止の場所であっても、荷物の積みおろしの場合に限って、時間に関係なく駐車とはならない。
questions.explanation:
ANSWER: FALSE / 不正解

WHY: The answer is **FALSE / 不正解** because this question is testing **Loading/unloading and the parking definition**, especially the parking rule. The governing rule is: A stop solely for loading or unloading that is completed within the statutory short period is treated differently from parking; a longer or continuing stop can become parking. The driver’s presence alone does not decide the issue. The statement changes, omits, or overstates a condition that the rule requires; that mismatch is the reason the statement is false.

RULE TO REMEMBER: A stop solely for loading or unloading that is completed within the statutory short period is treated differently from parking; a longer or continuing stop can become parking. The driver’s presence alone does not decide the issue.

PRACTICAL MEANING: Watch the time limit and purpose. “Any loading stop is never parking” is too broad.

EXAM TRAP: Watch the absolute wording “関係なく”. Japanese licence questions often become false because a limited rule is stated as an absolute rule.

questions.question_en: A two-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement of 125 cc or less is an ordinary motorcycle, so it may travel on an expressway.

The governing rule is: Motorcycles of 125 cc or less are not permitted on expressways. A machine being classified within the broader motorcycle licensing system does not make an under-125 cc vehicle expressway-eligible. questions.question_en: An ordinary automobile must not enter a priority lane for route buses if traffic is congested and there is a risk that the vehicle will be unable to leave the lane when a bus approaches.

questions.explanation:
ANSWER: TRUE / 正解

WHY: The answer is **TRUE / 正解** because this question is testing **Bus-priority lane**, especially the precise condition and wording used in the statement. The governing rule is: In a bus-priority lane, other vehicles may use the lane subject to the rule, but they must leave it promptly when a route bus approaches if they would obstruct it, and should not enter when congestion would prevent them from leaving. The statement applies that rule without changing the required condition, timing, distance, or exception, so the statement is correct.

RULE TO REMEMBER: In a bus-priority lane, other vehicles may use the lane subject to the rule, but they must leave it promptly when a route bus approaches if they would obstruct it, and should not enter when congestion would prevent them from leaving.

PRACTICAL MEANING: A priority lane is different from a bus-only lane.

EXAM TRAP: The exam is testing whether **Bus-priority lane** creates a prohibition, permission, or exception. Do not infer permission merely because the manoeuvre seems convenient or harmless.

questions.question_en: When a pedestrian is already crossing at a pedestrian crossing, a vehicle must stop, but if the pedestrian is only about to cross, the vehicle may proceed slowly.
